title: Conditional eosinophil suppression gave no clear incremental cross-cycle prediction of high CRP
abstract: In frozen NHANES 2005–2006 to separately sampled 2017–2018 adult prediction of CRP >10 mg/L, adding a neutrophil–eosinophil interaction changed weighted Brier loss by -0.000089813; target PSU 95% interval [-0.000234556, +0.000048060] and joint-refit interval [-0.000316107, +0.000161471] include zero. No clear incremental benefit was established beyond nonlinear leukocyte counts, NLR and demographic/body-size/smoking predictors. Frozen testing included 4,383 development and 4,827 confirmation complete-case adults. Code, public inputs, PSU bootstrap uncertainty, controls and author reruns accompany this scoped negative result. Both models overpredicted target prevalence; no clinical utility or physiological null is established.
